newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended mixed after 27 minutes of trade due to an electronic trading system failure.
Industrials were firm, lifted by a stronger rand, while golds fell on an ailing bullion price.
The system was halted twice on Wednesday, in the morning and in the afternoon, due to its inadequate performance on dealers systems, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said in a statement.
It said volume for the day was 208.3 million rand, about 40 percent of normal volumes.
"The market traded fast and furious during the second opening. Nearly 100 million shares were traded in the 10 minutes," a dealer said.
Dealers said the stronger rand boosted sentiment and futures players bought stock and sold futures.
They said there was interest in mining house stocks after the better-than-expected Anglo interim results on Tuesday.
Golds continued weak on an ailing bullion price which slipped below 373 per ounce and looked set to test lower levels.
"The gold price is quite low and the index is only down nine points. It is difficult to assess the underlying sentiment because there was little trade today," one dealer said.
Dealers said, barring a serious turn-about on Wall Street and the bullion price, industrials would continue strong on Wednesday and golds would weaken further.
The industrial index ended up 36 points to 8,051.4 points, the gold index was down 9.7 points to 1,563.7 points and the all-share index added 28.6 points to 6,749.9 points.
De Beers put on 125 cents to 139.25 rand, Anglo added 35 cents to 257.60 rand, Absa gained 50 cents to 24.50 rand and Nampak rose 85 cents to 19.10 rand.
Freegold lost a rand to 36 rand, Dries lost 10 cents to 53.40 rand, Kloof was down 25 cents to 38.25 rand.
Near-term industrial index futures were strong the back of a stronger rand and bonds. Gold contracts slipped below the 1,100 mark on a softer bullion price.
The December all-share contract was last at 6,235 from 6,170 settlement on Tuesday, the industrial contract was at 7,835/45 from 7,776 and the gold contract was at 1,067/77 from 1,110.
